judge.rationale: The candidate's runtime logic and tests are completely correct, properly summing token usage across rounds while handling missing round usage and preserving undefined when no round reports usage. However, it misses the acceptance criterion requiring the hook signature/type to make the aggregation unambiguous: `OrchestratorHooks.afterModelResponse` is left with `usage?: UsageMetadata` instead of renaming the parameter to `totalUsage?: UsageMetadata` (which the candidate's own `.lore/dod.md` even leaves unchecked). In `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`, the candidate also kept the new behavior under the 'Measured semantics — out of scope' section instead of moving it to the main specification section and updating `specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md` and `CLAUDE.md` as the reference did. Finally, the candidate introduces several extra files (`turnUsage.ts`, three separate test files, a new spec file, `.lore/dod.md`, and a modification to `scripts/lore-list-tests.mjs`) rather than keeping the helper and tests inline in `chatOrchestrator.ts` and `chatOrchestrator.test.ts`.
